- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days) are common; cap forecast at 10-15% above peak for next 3-5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) or mixed, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of past 10 days as baseline.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day exponential decay) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If last 3 sentiment values are all 0.67 or higher, forecast should be capped at 10% below recent 10-day high to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., 0.67 → -0.67), model often lags; adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
